memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The priest who offers it shall eat it; it is to be eaten in the sanctuary area, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting. Whatever touches any of the flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash it in the sanctuary area."'" - Lev 6:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The priest ate the sin offering. Strange as it sounds, he took the offering brought for another person's sin into himself.

The prophets saw something troubling in how Israel's priests came to treat this. Hosea accused them of feeding on the sins of my people and relishing their wickedness (Hos 4:8) — profiting from failure rather than grieving over it.

But at its best, this act pictured something profound. The priest identified with the sinner. He did not stand apart holding his nose. He took the offering that represented another's guilt and made it part of himself.

That is exactly what Christ did, and infinitely more. God made him who had no sin to be sin for us (2 Cor 5:21). He did not merely handle our guilt; He absorbed it. Hebrews says we do not have a high priest who is unable to empathise with our weaknesses (Heb 4:15).

And note the last detail: blood on a garment must be washed in the sanctuary area. Even the stains from handling sin were dealt with inside the holy place, not carried out into ordinary life.

Where sin has stained you, God has provided the washing — and it is found in His presence, not away from it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I stand apart from struggling people, or come alongside them?
2. Where do I take my stains — into hiding, or into God's presence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You took my sin into Yourself so that I could be made clean. Wash what has stained me, and teach me to carry others gently. Amen.
